subject: Latency regression observed (model-xi) — request for temporary SLA exception and fallback
messages:
From: Mike Barnes <mike.barnes@edgespark.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency spike observed p95 > SLA — model-xi (urgent)

Dylan,

We started seeing a sustained p95 spike against model-xi starting ~08:40 PDT this morning. Our customer-facing service is observing 650ms p95 for short prompts where our SLA is 250ms. This began after the model rollout on 2028-03-20 (model-xi-v1.2).

Attached is a small sample of request traces and histograms (latency-sample-20280329.csv) showing the regression pattern across regions, plus a couple of example request IDs. We need to request two things from Redwood urgently:

- Temporary SLA exception (we will need a carveout window while this is mitigated)
- Authorization to fallback to a quantized variant (model-xi-quant-v2) or an earlier pinned variant for up to 72 hours while EdgeSpark and Redwood assess root cause.

Can you confirm Redwood's proposed mitigation and any expected customer credits for the SLA miss? We need a quick path — customers are seeing impacts in production.

Thanks,

Mike Barnes
Director, Platform Ops | EdgeSpark
[Attachment: latency-sample-20280329.csv (text/csv)]

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency spike observed p95 > SLA — model-xi (initial triage)

Notes from triage (short):
- Observed same spike in our telemetry: p95 baseline ~230ms previous week, jumped to 600–700ms at 08:38 PDT.
- Correlation: higher token-cache eviction rates on the serving layer after the compilation change that shipped 2028-03-20 (kernel selection changes for attention op). Evidence: KV hit rate down ~18% and effective avg sequence handling increased.
- Impact surface: affects short-to-medium prompts; tail behavior worsened under bursty traffic.

Mitigation options (pros/cons):
1) Immediate rollback to xi-v1.1 (full rollback across their dedicated pool) — fastest route to restore latency, but requires coordination and a short reprovisioning window (15–30 min per shard).
2) Canary fallback to xi-quant-v2 (safe variant) with traffic split (start 10% -> 50%) — lower risk, minimal infra churn; quantized variant reduces cost and typically lowers execution time in our benchmarks, but we must validate quality differences for EdgeSpark's prompt set.
3) Apply temporary traffic cap for that tenant and request SLA carveout while we perform forensic and kernel revert/compile patch — short-term UX impact.

Estimated times: rollback ~1–2 hours full ops window; quantary fallback can be staged within 30 minutes but requires canary validation by QA (~45 min). I recommend: authorize immediate 10% canary fallback to xi-quant-v2 and approve a 72-hour SLA exception window while we monitor and decide to roll forward or rollback.

Telemetry links: https://console.redwood.ai/d/telemetry/edgespark?from=2028-03-28T00:00Z&to=2028-03-29T12:00Z
Request IDs included in attachment sample.

-naomi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: telemetry-snapshot-20280329.png (image/png)]

Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency spike observed p95 > SLA — model-xi (authorization)

Thanks for the fast triage. I authorize the following immediate steps for EdgeSpark (EDGE-4721):

1) Approve a 72-hour SLA exception window starting 2028-03-29T08:40Z to allow remediation work and monitoring. This exception must be documented in our contract system and we will finalize credits after post-mortem.
2) Authorize Naomi to initiate a staged canary fallback to model-xi-quant-v2 at 10% traffic immediately. If telemetry shows p95 under 300ms and quality checks pass, ramp to 50% within 2 hours.
3) If canary does not reduce p95 to acceptable range within 2 hours, proceed with rollback to xi-v1.1; Ops to coordinate downtime window no longer than 30 minutes per shard.

Ben — please draft the proposed credit posture for customer communications (suggest cap at 10% of monthly invoice for the affected window unless the post-mortem finds broader issues). Put a draft in the HubSpot ticket and route for legal once ready.

Dylan — notify EdgeSpark ops with these steps and the DocuSign amendment link. Naomi — proceed with canary and keep me updated every 30 minutes until p95 stabilizes.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
